identity.title: XR-1: Towards Versatile Vision-Language-Action Models via Learning Unified Vision-Motion Representations

problem.claim: VLA models must produce precise low-level actions from high-dimensional observations and transfer across heterogeneous robots and human demonstrations.

gap.claim: Existing latent-variable methods do not fully exploit complementary multimodal knowledge in large-scale heterogeneous datasets.

contributions.claim: XR-1 introduces Unified Vision-Motion Codes, a discrete latent representation jointly encoding visual dynamics and robotic motion via a dual-branch VQ-VAE.
It proposes three stages: self-supervised UVMC learning, cross-embodiment pretraining, and task-specific post-training.
The authors report validation across six robot embodiments and more than 120 manipulation tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present XR-1 as a novel versatile and scalable VLA framework centered on a unified vision-motion representation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report more than 12,000 real-world rollouts across six robot embodiments and over 120 manipulation tasks.
The authors report that XR-1 consistently outperforms π_0 and GR00T-N1.5, while generalizing to novel objects, backgrounds, distractors, and illumination changes.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper identifies precision and heterogeneous-domain transfer as two fundamental VLA challenges.
It attributes a limitation to insufficient use of complementary multimodal knowledge in existing latent-variable approaches.
XR-1 uses UVMC as an intermediate observation-action representation and aligns multimodal dynamics, trained in three stages.
The authors report extensive real-world testing and gains over named baselines with robustness to several distribution changes.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a representation design—joint vision-motion codes—to a staged training procedure and explicitly states the representation's roles between observations and actions and across heterogeneous data.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the proposed mechanism and its intended resolution of the stated gap easy to trace.
lessons.application: When presenting a multimodal method, map each representation component to a concrete bottleneck and show how training stages operationalize it.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method has no distinct intermediate representation or staged optimization.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, baseline values, task-wise breakdowns, or experimental conditions for the reported comparisons.
It does not specify how UVMC alignment or generalization was separately ablated.
